properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency of web3.js 4.16.0 (docs/package.json) pulled via web3-eth-accounts → ethereum-cryptography → @noble/curves 1.4.2: the secp256k1 ECDSA engine behind web3.eth.accounts.privateKeyToAccount and transaction signing, actually exercised by docs/index.js:22,26 (privateKeyToAccount for ETH and AVAX testnet senders). On EVM chains secp256k1 ECDSA is protocol-fixed (ecrecover precompile), so replacing it is a protocol-level change — observable here, not changeable in this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.6.1 ships under @ethersproject/signing-key; docs/package.json declares ethers ^5.7.2 alongside web3 4.16.0, so the ethers v5 tree (with its ECDSA sign/verify) is part of what this quickstart installs, whether or not index.js calls ethers directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic exposes ECDH key agreement alongside its ECDSA. Recorded as shipped-library capability: the docs quickstart image carries a classical ECDH implementation even though nothing in the repo's own code calls it. Quantum-unsafe key-agree primitive present in the dependency tree; migration ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pycryptodome 3.15.0 (requirements.txt:30) is the crypto provider for the web3.py toolchain: eth-hash uses it as the keccak backend for Web3.keccak in the anvil scripts, and eth-keyfile uses AES-128-CTR for web3 v3 keystore encryption. No direct AES call site in the repo's own code; the installed image ships AES-128/256 regardless. Quantum-safe cipher; 128-bit default is below the CNSA 2.0 AES-256 bar.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.4.0 (web3.js 4.16.0 tree) ships blake3 alongside sha2/sha3/keccak/scrypt. No blake3 call site in the repo's own code; recorded as shipped-library capability. BLAKE3 is quantum-safe (256-bit); no migration pressure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes 1.4.0 ships the scrypt KDF; web3-eth-accounts uses it for web3 v3 keystore (encrypt/decrypt) paths. scrypt-js 3.0.1 (separate roster object) covers the ethers v5 tree's copy of the same KDF. No direct scrypt call in repo code; recorded as shipped-library capability with its parameters unknown until a keystore call site exists.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes sha3/keccak is the hashing backbone of web3.js 4.16.0: docs/index.js:63,66 call web3.utils.keccak256 (event topic 'MessageSent(bytes)' + CCTP message hash), implemented over this package. Keccak-256 is quantum-safe at 128-bit Grover margin; no migration pressure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: requests 2.28.1 + urllib3 1.26.11 are declared for the web3.py toolchain (anvil integration tests import requests directly in crosschainTransferITV2.py). Any https:// RPC or API endpoint reached through web3.py's HTTPProvider or requests rides on these library defaults: TLS 1.2+, classical ECDHE key exchange, no post-quantum hybrid groups. The local anvil tests use plain http://0.0.0.0:8545, but the toolchain carries the TLS posture wherever it points at https.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pycryptodome 3.15.0 (requirements.txt:30) is the crypto provider for the anvil/web3.py toolchain: keccak backend for eth-hash (Web3.keccak in the integration tests), AES-128-CTR source for eth-keyfile (web3 v3 keystore), and it also ships 3DES/RSA/SHA-1/SHA-2 (covered by sibling roster objects). Changeable here — a requirements.txt bump.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js 3.0.1 (docs/package-lock.json:346) under @ethersproject/hdnode: the scrypt KDF for BIP39 mnemonic → seed and BIP32 HD-wallet derivation in the ethers v5 tree (docs/package.json declares ethers ^5.7.2). Recorded as shipped-library capability; no direct call site in repo code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.6.1 (docs/package-lock.json:562) is the elliptic-curve library of the ethers v5 tree (@ethersproject/signing-key): secp256k1 ECDSA sign/verify plus ECDH and other curves. docs/package.json declares ethers ^5.7.2, so this ships with the docs quickstart image. Quantum-unsafe ECDSA engine in the dependency tree; migration ML-DSA at the library level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js 1.1.7 (docs/package-lock.json:539,563) under @ethersproject/signing-key and sha2 in the ethers v5 tree: ships MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, keccak and other digest implementations. MD5/SHA-1 present in the shipped library is a posture fact even with no call site in repo code — recorded as shipped-library surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: docs/index.js:74 — Node global fetch() (undici) polling https://iris-api-sandbox.circle.com/attestations/… for CCTP attestation signatures. TLS on Node defaults: classical ECDHE key exchange (X25519/P-256), no PQ hybrid group unless a recent Node with them enabled is used — the repo pins no Node version (no .nvmrc/engines; Dockerfile is foundry-only), so PQ capability is unresolvable from the tree. This session carries CCTP message hashes and attestation signatures; harvest-now-decrypt-later app
